page.overview:
What is Poseidon?

Poseidon is the name of the primary sea-god of Classical Greek mythology. Later, in Roman mythology, Neptune was equated with it. For this reason, this article explains both gods.

Poseidon and Neptune have been mentioned in a handful of stories and poems, both those set in the Cthulhu Mythos and as references to their real-world aspects.

Poseidon was briefly mentioned in "To Greece, 1917," a tribute to the people and mythology of Classical Greece. (: "To Greece, 1917")

Father Neptune once appeared to Thomas Olney, holding a trident and accompanied by scores of tritons and nereids, as well as the primal god Nodens. (: "The Strange High House in the Mist")
